name: Conventional activated sludge
principle: The workhorse municipal process: primary-settled sewage is aerated with return activated sludge so a flocculent mixed community oxidises BOD and nitrifies ammonia; secondary clarification separates sludge, part returned as RAS, part wasted. Commodity process knowledge; vendors supply aeration and clarification equipment.

costs.metric: capital cost, extended-aeration activated sludge package plant, per gallon per day of capacity (plants above 0.02 MGD)
costs.basis: EPA fact sheet, figure as published: for larger plants capital costs are approximately USD 2 to USD 2.50 per gallon of wastewater treated. Sheet dated September 2000 and states no dollar year, so the document year is recorded.

source.note: US EPA, Wastewater Technology Fact Sheet: Package Plants, EPA 832-F-00-016, September 2000, COSTS section (extended-aeration package plants; figures provided by Aeration Products, Inc.)

costs.metric: capital cost, extended-aeration activated sludge package plant, per gallon per day of capacity (plants below 0.02 MGD)
costs.basis: Smaller extended-aeration package plants designed for less than 0.02 MGD cost approximately USD 4 to USD 6 per gallon of water treated, based on capital costs; routine maintenance averages USD 350 per year. Document year recorded; no dollar year stated in the sheet.

source.note: US EPA, Wastewater Technology Fact Sheet: Package Plants, EPA 832-F-00-016, September 2000, COSTS section (extended-aeration package plants; figures provided by Aeration Products, Inc.)

gaps.item: operating cost and energy demand per m3 treated, with dollar year and basis
gaps.reason: Package-plant capital cost per gallon per day is now recorded (EPA 832-F-00-016, 2000 basis). Operating cost and specific energy for a full-size activated sludge plant are not stated in any source read.

where.hint: EPA fact sheets state no operating energy figure for activated sludge; plant energy benchmarks are in utility and WEF publications
